programme: RELA (NF-κB p65) drives inflammatory/survival transcription, ATF2 supplies the parallel stress-kinase (JNK/p38-linked) AP-1 output, BACH1 represses the redox/antioxidant arm (HMOX1, NQO1) that normally counterbalances this signaling, PIN1 potentiates these phospho-dependent transcription factors by prolyl isomerization and also directly modulates huntingtin turnover, and NPM1 acts as the nucleolar-stress sensor feeding into the same response. Together these five form a chronic cellular-stress transcription module, not a single physical complex.
role_in_a: In Huntington's disease this module is engaged by mutant-huntingtin proteotoxicity: NPM1-sensed nucleolar stress tracks HD progression and controls mutant-huntingtin toxicity, RELA/NF-κB co-regulates cytokine and endocannabinoid signaling and miRNA transcription in HD models, BACH1/NRF2 dual-activity compounds are being explored as candidate HD therapeutics, and PIN1 directly modulates huntingtin levels and aggregate accumulation. ATF2's placement here is weaker, resting on a single staging/bioinformatic study rather than a mechanistic one.
role_in_b: In melanoma the same core factors appear in oncogenic-stress and therapy-response contexts: RELA/NF-κB-driven chromatin remodeling accompanies drug-induced dedifferentiation, a PLK1-BACH1 axis promotes melanoma progression in mouse models, and a FAK/SRC-JNK-ATF2 axis regulates ferroptosis. PIN1 and NPM1 have no melanoma-specific paper in this record, even though both score highly on Open Targets association (0.857 and 0.966 respectively), so their role here is inferred from general Open Targets placement rather than documented mechanism.
shared_axis: Both diseases are states of sustained cellular stress in long-lived or stress-exposed cells — proteotoxic/nucleolar stress from misfolded huntingtin in HD, oncogenic/UV/therapy-induced stress in melanoma — and both would be expected to lean on the same core stress-transcription module (NF-κB, AP-1/ATF2, BACH1-controlled redox repression, PIN1-amplified phosphosignaling) even though the upstream trigger differs entirely between a neurodegenerative and a malignant process.
reasoning: The module is biologically nameable and internally coherent (NF-κB/AP-1/redox-stress signaling amplified by PIN1, sensed via nucleolar stress), and each disease separately has on-point literature for at least part of it — RELA and BACH1 are the only two factors placed in both diseases, but never jointly. PIN1 and NPM1 are grounded only in HD, and ATF2's HD paper is associative rather than mechanistic, so the HD–melanoma connection itself is reasoned rather than retrieved, which caps this at moderate rather than strong. Counts also favor caution: the two highest-recurrence factors overall (KAT7, ARID4A at 123/189) carry no disease-specific record at all and had to be left out of the story.
support: PMID 24360910 (RELA co-regulates cytokine/endocannabinoid systems in HD models); PMID 25757558 (RELA/p65 regulates miRNA transcription in HD mouse tissue); PMID 41986344 (RELA/NF-κB drives chromatin remodeling in drug-induced melanoma dedifferentiation); PMID 32863231 (dual BACH1/NRF2-active compounds proposed for HD); PMID 41284701 (PLK1-BACH1 axis promotes melanoma progression in mice); PMID 33049985 (ATF2 associated with HD symptomatic-transition staging, associative only); PMID 41862445 (ATF2/FAK-SRC-JNK axis regulates ferroptosis in melanoma models); PMID 28533744 (PIN1 modulates huntingtin levels/aggregation in vitro); PMID 34880223 (NPM1-linked nucleolar stress controls mutant-huntingtin toxicity); PMID 27510036 (NPM1 regulates neuronal survival, HD-relevant model).
how_to_falsify: In parallel, treat a mutant-huntingtin neuronal/patient-iPSC model and a MAPK-inhibitor-stressed or UV-stressed melanoma line with a PIN1 inhibitor (e.g. sulfopin/juglone) or PIN1 knockdown, then measure RELA- and ATF2-target induction (e.g. IL6, CDKN1A) and BACH1 target derepression (HMOX1, NQO1) by qPCR/ChIP in both systems. If PIN1 loss blunts this stress-transcription signature in one disease model but not the other, the shared-module account is wrong; if huntingtin aggregation and melanoma dedifferentiation/ferroptosis phenotypes shift independently of this signature, the account is falsified.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|skin, so HD-side evidence reflects peripheral/whole-blood or model-system signatures, not brain tissue directly — claims about neuronal proteotoxic stress are extrapolated. 189 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so apparent robustness may partly reflect within-cohort pseudoreplication rather than independent replication. Six of the eleven concordant factors (KAT7, ARID4A, ZGPAT, ZBTB33, ZNF335, ABL1) were excluded from the account despite meeting the recurrence threshold because no disease-specific record ties them to HD or melanoma here — notably ARID4A's target list (RB1, SIN3A, BRMS1) suggests a distinct SIN3A-corepressor story that this record simply does not support for this pair. The single-view exclusions (TCF7L1, LEF1, ZNF503, PITX2, etc.) rule out any WNT/pluripotency-factor narrative, and the tissue-generic exclusions (ETS1, LEF1, IRF7, DNMT1, FOXM1, TCF7) mean this account is not simply restating generic blood/skin proliferation or interferon biology. No PMID in the record discusses Huntington's disease and melanoma jointly.
